output.title: Check data residency before you automate
output.body:
Before you automate a workflow, make data residency the first control, not a footnote. In plain English, residency means where the data is allowed to live and move: on your own system, in a specific country, or inside a vendor service. For an owner-operator, the real question is not “can AI do this?” but “which parts of this one recurring workflow are allowed to leave my environment at all?”

Take a workflow you already handle by hand, such as customer-data entry, invoice processing, or lead follow-up. Mark the fields that should stay put because of contract terms, policy, or basic caution: payment details, personal data, internal pricing, or supplier-only information. Then read the tool’s service agreement and data-handling docs. If the tool cannot keep those fields where you need them, that workflow is not ready for that automation path, no matter how tidy the demo looks.

That is the bounded decision: not “AI or no AI,” but “what can move, and what must stay local?” If most of the workflow can move, a pilot may make sense. If everything must stay on-premise, you are looking at a self-hosted or tightly integrated approach. Less glamorous than a launch video, but more useful on Monday.
